channel.title: Project Syndicate
channel.description: Project Syndicate commentary, each entry with its lead image and photo credit, the summary, the full byline and a clean link to the article. The articles themselves are paywalled and are not reproduced.

item.title: Trump’s Great Oil Heist
item.dc:creator: Cristina Ramirez
item.description: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth. Billions in US and foreign investment could strengthen the chavista regime and give future American presidents powerful incentives to preserve the political status quo.
item.content:encoded:
Photo: Jesus Vargas/Getty Images

Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth. Billions in US and foreign investment could strengthen the chavista regime and give future American presidents powerful incentives to preserve the political status quo.

Read the full commentary on Project Syndicate

item.title: Global AI Oversight Now
item.dc:creator: Gabriela Ramos
item.description: AI is already concentrating enormous economic power and deepening existing inequalities, yet governments lack the institutions and expertise needed to govern it. They should establish an international AI body that can set standards and coordinate a collective response to threats no country can handle alone.
item.content:encoded:
Photo: Angela Weiss/AFP via Getty Images

AI is already concentrating enormous economic power and deepening existing inequalities, yet governments lack the institutions and expertise needed to govern it. They should establish an international AI body that can set standards and coordinate a collective response to threats no country can handle alone.

item.title: Climate Resilience Starts With Care
item.dc:creator: Caren Grown and Kendall Trelegan
item.description: Climate shocks can disrupt services that millions of vulnerable people rely on, yet care is largely absent from adaptation plans and national funding estimates. Investing in climate-resilient care can prevent cascading health and economic crises while creating jobs and easing pressure on public budgets.
item.content:encoded:
Photo: Munir Uz Zaman/AFP via Getty Images

Climate shocks can disrupt services that millions of vulnerable people rely on, yet care is largely absent from adaptation plans and national funding estimates. Investing in climate-resilient care can prevent cascading health and economic crises while creating jobs and easing pressure on public budgets.

item.title: Conserving a Connected Ocean
item.dc:creator: Marie-May Jeremie
item.description: For Seychelles and other countries across the Western Indian Ocean region, marine conservation is a fundamental component of national development. But the ocean observes no national borders, which makes international cooperation and common financing instruments essential.

item.title: Why Is the Global Economy So Resilient?
item.dc:creator: Nouriel Roubini
item.description: With the global economy having weathered major trade and energy shocks over the past two years, growth should improve in 2027, and inflation should fall. Although various political and policy-driven risks could change the outlook, they remain less likely than the relatively benign baseline scenario.
item.content:encoded:
Photo: Hassan Ghaedi/Anadolu via Getty Images

With the global economy having weathered major trade and energy shocks over the past two years, growth should improve in 2027, and inflation should fall. Although various political and policy-driven risks could change the outlook, they remain less likely than the relatively benign baseline scenario.

item.title: Closing Europe’s Dynamism Deficit
item.dc:creator: Carl Benedikt Frey
item.description: Europe has built an economic framework that protects yesterday’s champions at the expense of tomorrow’s potential winners. To remain competitive, sovereign, and secure in the 21st century, it will need a new model geared toward promoting domestic innovation and commercialization at scale.
item.content:encoded:
Photo: J Studios/Getty Images

Europe has built an economic framework that protects yesterday’s champions at the expense of tomorrow’s potential winners. To remain competitive, sovereign, and secure in the 21st century, it will need a new model geared toward promoting domestic innovation and commercialization at scale.

item.title: America’s Looming Debt Reckoning
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Rogoff
item.description: High debt levels become dangerous when rising interest rates push up borrowing costs and governments fail to respond. With little political appetite to rein in its federal deficit and ballooning debt, the United States risks finding itself with few options when the next war, recession, or financial crisis arrives.
item.content:encoded:
Photo: Derek White/Getty Images for the Peter G. Peterson Foundation

High debt levels become dangerous when rising interest rates push up borrowing costs and governments fail to respond. With little political appetite to rein in its federal deficit and ballooning debt, the United States risks finding itself with few options when the next war, recession, or financial crisis arrives.

item.title: The OECD Should Be Reclaimed, Not Abandoned
item.dc:creator: Kim Ruhl and Pierre Yared
item.description: In recent years, the OECD has strayed from its core mission of coordinating economic policy among the US and its allies, instead building programs around gender budgeting and environmental justice. The Trump administration should use its leverage at the organization to return its focus to economics and national security.
item.content:encoded:
Photo: Joel Saget/AFP via Getty Images

In recent years, the OECD has strayed from its core mission of coordinating economic policy among the US and its allies, instead building programs around gender budgeting and environmental justice. The Trump administration should use its leverage at the organization to return its focus to economics and national security.

item.title: Putin Is Testing NATO at Ukraine’s Borders
item.dc:creator: Anna Husarska
item.description: The Kremlin is determined to isolate Ukraine, which means not only breaking the will of the country’s backers, but also cutting it off physically by striking merchant ships, ports, and border crossings. These assaults cannot go unanswered, because they embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin to continue testing the West.

item.title: The Hard Road to a Middle-Power Order
item.dc:creator: Sophie Eisentraut
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has challenged the world’s middle powers to build a better international order. Yet they are increasingly turning to coalitions of the willing and a patchwork of separate initiatives that risk entrenching zero-sum mindsets and making collective action harder.

item.title: The Sovereign Wealth Fund America Needs
item.dc:creator: Steven Hill and John Menke
item.description: Two recent proposals to establish a new US sovereign wealth fund would fail to make good on a good idea, because neither plan would produce a fund nearly large enough to meet America’s mounting financing needs. But a different approach, funded by Treasury sales, could.
item.content:encoded:
Photo: Arno Burgi/picture alliance via Getty Images

Two recent proposals to establish a new US sovereign wealth fund would fail to make good on a good idea, because neither plan would produce a fund nearly large enough to meet America’s mounting financing needs. But a different approach, funded by Treasury sales, could.

item.title: Trump’s Vanity Summit With Xi
item.dc:creator: Stephen S. Roach
item.description: While expectations for the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were low, it was disappointing to watch them prioritize pageantry over substance. Trump’s cringe-worthy declarations of heartfelt admiration for Xi reflect his twisted sense that the trappings of power are power itself.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Human Rights and Populist Wrongs
item.dc:creator: Murray Hunt
item.description: For the first time, all the UK’s political parties on the right favor withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights. But the story of the Hillsborough Law shows how human-rights laws, not least the ECHR, help ordinary people hold the state accountable for its costliest failings.

item.title: Is Another Eurozone Debt Crisis Looming?
item.dc:creator: Desmond Lachman
item.description: At a time when the cost of servicing sovereign debt is rising globally, France stands out as an especially fragile case. Its public debt-to-GDP ratio is edging up toward that of Greece on the eve of its sovereign-debt crisis, and the French political system seems unable to do anything about it.
item.content:encoded:
Photo: Lou Benoist/AFP via Getty Images

item.title: Will AI Reverse the Renminbi’s Rise?
item.dc:creator: Miao Yanliang
item.description: In China, AI-driven productivity gains will most likely be in non-tradable services, which could push down relative prices and put downward pressure on the renminbi’s real exchange rate. To ensure that this does not also mean lower income and weaker demand, policymakers should ensure that the productivity dividend is broadly shared.
item.content:encoded:
Photo: Cheng Xin/Getty Images

To ensure that this does not also mean lower income and weaker demand, policymakers should ensure that the productivity dividend is broadly shared.

item.title: The Price of You
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Owens
item.description: As more people shop online, firms are increasingly setting individualized prices based on personal data, including purchase history, location, demographics, behavior, and biometric data. AI threatens to turbocharge such surveillance pricing, further widening the gap between privacy expectations and reality.

item.title: Investing in Brain Health
item.dc:creator: Harris Eyre
item.description: Just as AI agents are mastering complex cognitive tasks, our own ability to perform the same tasks is eroding. Whether AI vindicates its boosters or fizzles out like the Metaverse craze of 2022, we will not fare well without a civilization-wide effort to rebuild the cognitive skills that make technological progress possible.

item.title: Europe Still Needs Molecules
item.dc:creator: Ana Palacio
item.description: Not even the most effective European electrification strategy will eliminate the need for the molecules that fossil fuels provide. Given this, Europe must diversify its oil and gas supplies, maintain its refining capacity, and lock in decarbonization by building a hydrogen-energy industry at scale.

item.title: Energy Security in an Age of Disruption
item.dc:creator: Diego Hernandez Diaz
item.description: While there is no single prescription for energy security, strengthening “response capacity,” such as by establishing stockpiles, substituting sources, and diversifying suppliers, is essential. The point is not to eliminate vulnerabilities altogether, but to ensure that there are options when disruption arrives.

item.title: Africa’s Common Currency-in-Waiting
item.dc:creator: Hippolyte Fofack
item.description: While the phased approach of the Economic Community of West African States to implementing a long-delayed single currency will maintain momentum without compromising macroeconomic discipline, the bloc still lacks a robust mechanism to address asymmetric shocks. That is why fiscal integration must come first.
